data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew 'yardan', meaning 'Jewess'. Derived from the name 'Yarden', meaning 'flowing down'. In the Bible, Yarden is the name of the Jordan River. The name Yardena carries the meaning “Jewess, light one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Yardena usually hope their child will grow to embody jewess, light one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual growth and renewal, like the flowing water of the river.
data.etymology: Yardena belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jewess, light one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yardena total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: In the 1st century AD, the New Testament of the Bible mentions a woman named Yardena, or Salome, who is the daughter of Herodias and dances for King Herod during his birthday feast. She requests the head of John the Baptist as a reward for her dance, which Herod grants despite his initial reluctance. This episode is described in Mark 6:21-28.

In the 5th century AD, during the Byzantine Empire, there was a monastery located in the region of Galilee, Israel, dedicated to Saint Yardena. According to tradition, Saint Yardena was a local woman who lived during the time of Jesus and was a devoted follower. She was believed to have performed miracles and was later venerated as a saint. The monastery was an important center of pilgrimage for Christians in the region.
